chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yunus, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
It is permissible for the sick person to recite in the obligatory prayer only Fatihat al-Kitab, and it is permissible for the healthy person in making up the supererogatory prayer by night and day.

key_terms.اللَّيْلِ: the night, referring to night supererogatory prayers
key_terms.النَّهَارِ: the day, referring to day supererogatory prayers
key_terms.الْمَرِيضِ: the sick person whose condition affects the normal prayer ruling
key_terms.فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ: Surat al-Fatihah, recited here by itself
key_terms.قَضَاءِ: making up a missed act of worship

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to recite only Fatihat al-Kitab in obligatory or make-up supererogatory prayers?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning recitation in prayer. It permits the sick person in an obligatory prayer to recite only Fatihat al-Kitab, and it also permits the healthy person the same in making up supererogatory prayers of the night and day.
